raw.markdown:
To get Google Search data via an API, you have to choose between official Google APIs or third-party Search Engine Results Page (SERP) APIs depending on whether you want to search the entire web or analyze your own site's performance.

Importantly, Google’s traditional Custom Search JSON API is retiring on January 1, 2027, and is completely closed to new sign-ups. [0](https://developers.google.com/custom-search/v1/overview) [8](https://brave.com/learn/google-api-shutdown/)

Here are the best current options available:

## 1. Official Google APIs (For Specific Use Cases)

- Google Search Console API: Best if you own a website and need to pull your own search traffic data. It provides organic search impressions, clicks, keywords, and rankings for your verified properties.
- Vertex AI Search: Google's recommended alternative for building structured search applications. It allows you to programmatically search across up to 50 specified domains or your own dataset.
- Google Places API (Text Search): Best for retrieving local business listings, map coordinates, and review data using text-based queries (e.g., "coffee shops in Los Angeles").

## 2. Third-Party SERP APIs (For Global Web Search Data)

Because Google does not offer a public, full-web search API for scrapers and SEO tools, specialized providers handle the infrastructure, global proxies, and JavaScript rendering required to pull real-time results. [3](https://serpapi.com/) [5](https://github.com/luminati-io/google-search-api)

API Provider | Standout Feature | Supported Formats
--- | --- | ---
SerpApi | Highly accurate geo-location proxying; parses Maps, Local, and Shopping. | JSON
Bright Data Search API | Enterprise-grade scale; built-in JavaScript rendering to bypass bot detection. | JSON, HTML, Markdown
SearchApi | Real-time SERP tracking with lightning-fast response times. | JSON

raw.markdown:
To get Google Search data via an API, you have to choose between official Google APIs or third-party Search Engine Results Page (SERP) APIs depending on whether you want to search the entire web or analyze your own site's performance.

Importantly, Google’s traditional Custom Search JSON API is retiring on January 1, 2027, and is completely closed to new sign-ups. [0](https://developers.google.com/custom-search/v1/overview) [8](https://brave.com/learn/google-api-shutdown/)

Here are the best current options available:

## 1. Official Google APIs (For Specific Use Cases)

- Google Search Console API: Best if you own a website and need to pull your own search traffic data. It provides organic search impressions, clicks, keywords, and rankings for your verified properties.
- Vertex AI Search: Google's recommended alternative for building structured search applications. It allows you to programmatically search across up to 50 specified domains or your own dataset.
- Google Places API (Text Search): Best for retrieving local business listings, map coordinates, and review data using text-based queries (e.g., "coffee shops in Los Angeles").

## 2. Third-Party SERP APIs (For Global Web Search Data)

Because Google does not offer a public, full-web search API for scrapers and SEO tools, specialized providers handle the infrastructure, global proxies, and JavaScript rendering required to pull real-time results. [3](https://serpapi.com/) [5](https://github.com/luminati-io/google-search-api)

API Provider | Standout Feature | Supported Formats
--- | --- | ---
SerpApi | Highly accurate geo-location proxying; parses Maps, Local, and Shopping. | JSON
Bright Data Search API | Enterprise-grade scale; built-in JavaScript rendering to bypass bot detection. | JSON, HTML, Markdown
SearchApi | Real-time SERP tracking with lightning-fast response times. | JSON

To help point you in the exact right direction, tell me a bit more about your project:

- Are you trying to scrape public web results for SEO/market research, or pull data for a website you own?
- What programming language (e.g., Python, Node.js) are you planning to use?
- What volume of searches do you expect to make daily?
